title: A store that survives Buen Fin
summary: An artisan cooperative from Tlaquepaque gets ten times its usual traffic during Buen Fin. The store must grow on its own and keep selling if a zone fails.

requirements.1: {{s1}} is each individual server: it has its own operating system the team patches, its inventory agent installed, and runs all day.
requirements.2: {{s2}} keeps 2 to 20 copies across both zones, adds or removes them with the load and replaces the ones that fail.
requirements.3: {{s3}} receives and decrypts HTTPS, sends /api to one group and /tienda to another, and only forwards to healthy servers.
requirements.4: {{s4}} issues and automatically renews what slot 3 presents to the browser to prove it is tienda.mx.
requirements.5: {{s5}} records CPU every minute and alerts the on-call team if it stays above 80 % for 5 minutes.
requirements.6: The managed database stores orders and inventory, and only the slot 1 servers query it.

s1.explanation: Amazon EC2 provides instances with a full operating system: the team patches them, installs its agent and they run with no time limit. Lambda gives no operating system access and stops each run at 15 minutes.

s2.explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling group keeps capacity between the minimum and maximum, spreads instances across zones, scales with the load and replaces instances that fail their health check. A launch template only describes how to launch them.

s3.explanation: The Application Load Balancer terminates TLS, sends /api and /tienda to different target groups with path rules and only forwards to targets that pass their health check. The Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and does not read the URL.
s3.hint_cue: sends /api to one group and /tienda to another

s4.explanation: The ALB presents an X.509 certificate that proves the domain; ACM issues the public one for tienda.mx and renews it automatically while it is in use and its validation CNAME stays in DNS. KMS stores keys, not certificates.
s4.hint_cue: presents to the browser to prove it is tienda.mx

s5.explanation: CloudWatch receives the instance CPU every minute and an alarm moves to ALARM when it stays above 80 % for 5 minutes; its action alerts the on-call team. Trusted Advisor only runs periodic checks.

aws-lambda.s1: Lambda stops each run at 15 minutes and does not let the team patch the operating system or install agents.

aws-launch-template.s2: A launch template is only the template with the AMI and instance type: it does not keep copies or replace the ones that fail.

aws-nlb.s3: The Network Load Balancer works at layer 4: it spreads TCP connections but does not read the URL to send /api and /tienda to different groups.

aws-kms.s4: KMS creates and controls keys to encrypt and sign data, but the ALB presents an X.509 certificate, which ACM issues and renews.

aws-trusted-advisor.s5: Trusted Advisor gives periodic best-practice recommendations; it does not measure CPU every minute or alert the on-call team.
